rows.why: The defining feature is buttons arranged in doubled pairs down the front placket rather than evenly spaced singles. Upscaling the drawing shows one collar button at the placket top followed by five tightly-spaced PAIRS. The photo shows the same construction: a neck button, then three complete pairs (two buttons nearly touching, ~50px apart, with ~300px between groups) plus the first button of a fourth pair at the bottom crop line. That grouping is unmistakable and cannot be confused with siblings btn-6/7/8/9, which are all single-button plackets. Confidence is medium only because the mid-chest crop cuts off groups 4 and 5, so the literal count of five is inferred rather than seen; the visible spacing is consistent with five, and nothing contradicts the drawing. Noted but not disqualifying: the buttons are sewn with red cross-stitch thread, which literalizes the drawing's red annotation markers - a styling quirk, not a construction mismatch.

Drawing carries a printed 85.00 degree callout with leader arrows onto the two collar point tips; the callout convention was independently validated on french-in-8cm (printed 145, drawing measured 151). Drawing shows pointed tips, no tip buttons, one band button; photo matches on family and button configuration. Photo spread off a 50px-gridded render: vertex (405,505), tips (250,690) and (625,665), giving 40 and 54 degree half-angles, total 94 vs drawn 85. The 14 degree asymmetry shows the model is rotated off-axis so this is 94 plus or minus 10. Across all ten leafed photos measured the same way the apparent-spread ranking matched the drawn-callout ranking monotonically. DEFECT: necktie plus fastened throat button completely conceal the collar band.

Button count contradiction. At 16x nearest-neighbour raw-pixel zoom of both collar leaves, button-down-collar-with-78cm-stand.jpg has NO button anywhere on either leaf; its only button is a single throat button on the band, inside the triangular gap where the leaves cross. The convention is verified inside the family: point-in-7cm-with-button.jpg, at identical scale and viewpoint, draws a distinct 4px circle on each leaf just above the tip PLUS the throat button, so this illustrator does draw tip buttons when they exist. The photo shows tip buttons on BOTH points (left ~(320,720), right ~(755,715), each confirmed at 4x) and hides the band and its throat button entirely behind a necktie. The photo adds two buttons the drawing lacks and conceals the one it has. Secondary and weaker: the drawing prints 90.00 degrees and measures ~95 as drawn, while the photo projects 76.9 degrees with a 5.9 degree left/right asymmetry as the error bar. ESCALATE THE DRAWING TOO: a file named button-down-collar that draws no button-down is a source defect. Also note 7.8 cm is not a plausible collar-stand height - real stands run 3-4.5 cm - so that number looks like a point length mis-filed as a stand.

The drawing's printed callout reads 0.1cm, contradicting the row's 0.3 cm label, and the drawing wins.
